summary:
The Autism Collaboration, Accountability, Research, Education, and Support Act of 2024 (Autism CARES Act of 2024) amends the Public Health Service Act to expand and reauthorize federal autism spectrum disorder research, surveillance, education, intervention, coordination, and reporting activities through FY2029, and creates a discretionary technical-assistance authority regarding communication supports.

Section 2 amends PHSA § 409C, 42 U.S.C. § 284g, governing National Institutes of Health autism activities. It requires NIH, in consultation with relevant federal departments and agencies as appropriate, to support expanded basic and clinical research fields, expressly including psychiatry, psychology, developmental behavioral pediatrics, audiology, and gerontology; to address interventions, services and supports across the lifespan, co-occurring conditions, caregiver supports, and the full range of support and service needs. It adds gerontology to the disciplines for autism Centers of Excellence, increases the minimum number of centers from five to seven, revises the public-input provision to require mechanisms for information access and comment, and authorizes NIH guidance to centers on engagement with individuals with autism spectrum disorder and specified stakeholders. New § 409C(e) requires the NIH Director, for FY2026–FY2029, to submit directly to the President for review and transmittal to Congress an annual budget estimate for NIH initiatives pursuant to the Interagency Autism Coordinating Committee strategic plan, after opportunity for comment by the Secretary and IACC without change.

Section 3 amends PHSA §§ 399AA–399EE, 42 U.S.C. §§ 280i–280i-4. It reauthorizes the developmental disabilities surveillance and research program in § 399AA through September 30, 2029, adds “across the lifespan,” and makes terminology changes for Indian Tribes and Tribal organizations. It amends § 399BB to require culturally and linguistically appropriate information, expand references to screening and diagnostic tools, revise “higher risk” to “increased likelihood,” authorize consideration of parent and guardian perspectives, strengthen State autism and developmental-disabilities programs, require certain program sites to provide culturally and linguistically appropriate services, and revise intervention research authority to promote grants or contracts to develop, evaluate, issue guidelines for, and disseminate evidence-based practices addressing physical, behavioral health, and communication needs across the lifespan. It requires, within two years of enactment, a report on the need for and feasibility of expanding developmental-behavioral pediatrician training programs, and reauthorizes § 399BB through September 30, 2029.

Section 3 also amends IACC duties in § 399CC to require regular activities, a strategic plan with proposed budgetary requirements and anti-duplication recommendations, annual updates on advances, biennial strategic-plan updates, and reauthorization through September 30, 2029. It amends § 399DD to require, within four years after September 30, 2024, a publicly available progress report, revise the mental-health report requirements, and require within two years an update on young adults and transition to adulthood. Section 399EE authorizes appropriations, not direct appropriations, for FY2025–FY2029: $28.1 million for § 399AA, $56.344 million for § 399BB, and $306 million for § 409C.

Section 4 authorizes the Secretary of Health and Human Services, upon request of a State, Indian Tribe, Tribal organization, locality, or territory, to provide training and technical assistance on use of HHS-administered federal funding for evidence-based communication services, tools, and technologies, and requires an annual report to specified congressional committees.
